Detection probability from every water cell to every receiver

Source: R/de_field.R
de_field.Rd

Evaluates a detection model at the distance through water between each receiver and each water cell, for one tag model and one date. The result is the per-transmission detection probability that the location likelihood uses, stored on the logit scale.

Usage

de_field(distances, model, depth = NULL, tag_model = NULL, date = NULL)

Arguments

distances

A water_distances() table.

model

A de_model().

depth

Receiver depth in metres, the depth_m the model reads: one number for every receiver, or a vector named by receiver key. By default the deploy_z column of the receivers given to water_distances(), or NA when there was none.

tag_model

The tag model, for a model that reads tag_model.

date

One date, a Date or a POSIXct in UTC, at which the model's modulators are evaluated. Needed only when a modulator is a function.

Value

An object of class de_field, a list with:

  • eta: a matrix of logits, one row per water cell and one column per receiver. field$p returns the same matrix on the probability scale, computed when asked for.

  • cells: the terra cell numbers of the rows.

  • receivers: the receiver keys of the columns.

  • key: "station_id" or "receiver_serial", the column the keys come from.

  • lookup: receiver serials, stations and deployment times when water_distances() had them, else NULL.

  • receiver_xy: the key and the position (x, y, in the CRS of the grid) used for each receiver.

  • grid, model, distances, and inputs, a list holding depth, tag_model, date and the modulator values used.

as.data.frame() gives one row per pair in distances, with columns cell, the receiver key, distance_m, in_water, eta and p. field$p and field[["p"]] give the probability matrix.

Details

A pair that no water path connects, or that water_distances() left out beyond max_distance, has a logit of -Inf: the receiver cannot hear that cell. A pair whose straight line meets land gets the model's blocked offset added to its logit; see de_model(). With blocked = 0, a message counts the pairs with land between them that the curve still gives a detection probability of 0.05 or more.

See also

system_de() for the probability that the array detects a transmission from each cell; plot.de_field().

Examples

# The Stoney example: Stoney Lake (100 m cells, land NA) and 70 receivers.
tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Pairs beyond 2 km are left out: there every receiver hears less than 1e-4.
d <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000)
# The curve of the Stoney example; each receiver reads it at its own depth,
# deploy_z.
curve <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(d, curve)
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
field
#> <de_field> 4,818 water cells x 70 receivers (by station_id)
#>   model: de_logistic, d50 250/750 m, d05 500/1500 m, depths 1/35 m
#>   blocked line of sight: 9,283 of 49,214 pairs, curve read at the
#>     distance through water
#>   cells with p >= 0.05 per receiver: median 101, range 40 to 265
range(field$p[, "S005"])
#> [1] 0.00 0.95
head(as.data.frame(field))
#>    cell station_id distance_m in_water       eta            p
#> 1 17483       S001   1968.380    FALSE -18.13111 1.335859e-08
#> 2 17651       S001   1871.543    FALSE -17.09427 3.767510e-08
#> 3 17652       S001   1911.151    FALSE -17.51835 2.465338e-08
#> 4 17653       S001   1957.381    FALSE -18.01333 1.502824e-08
#> 5 17819       S001   1778.762    FALSE -16.10086 1.017388e-07
#> 6 17820       S001   1821.723    FALSE -16.56084 6.422698e-08
